summary: Intermittent throughput pulses on Dedicated pool causing p99 spikes and evictions
description:
Issue summary: Customer AtlasAI reports recurring throughput 'pulses' on their Dedicated pool leading to p99 latency spikes and sporadic allocation evictions.
Impact: Multiple customer routes experienced 5-20% reduction in sustained throughput during pulses and transient p99 latency jumps from ~120ms to 1.8s. Some in-flight requests returned 503/504 during eviction windows.
Environment: prod-us-west-2, Dedicated pool id dp-84a2 (AtlasAI reserved pool), workload: many short-lived streaming inferences and periodic long-context prefix caching jobs.
Steps to reproduce:
1) Send mix of short chat streams (50-200 tokens) at steady 100 qps and intermittent long warmup requests (10k token KV cache warmup) every 5 minutes.
2) Observe autoscaler and scheduler metrics in Grafana and pool allocation log.
Observed behavior:
- Pool throughput and GPU attach rate shows periodic 3-7 minute pulses where free GPU slots drop and evictions increase.
- Autoscaler reacts by spinning new nodes then quickly shrinking, causing oscillation and fragmentation.
- NVMe/PCIe io_wait and host-side memory pressure correlate with pulses.
Expected behavior: Stable throughput with autoscaler smoothing reactive decisions; no eviction spikes when occasional warmup jobs run.
Logs/snippets:
- Grafana traces: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/pool-dp-84a2?orgId=1
- Sample scheduler log lines: "evicting allocation tenant=atlasai job=kv-prefetch size=9.3GB reason=memory_pressure"
- Host metrics: pcie_io_wait spikes to 85% during pulses.
Attachments: customer-provided client traces and request IDs included in comments.
comments: Aisha Kumar (Support) 2026-03-10: Opened ticket after AtlasAI reported repeated p99 spikes this morning. Requesting immediate triage. Included sample request IDs: req_20260310_1452_{a,b,c}.
Drew Patel (SRE) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged. Pulling pool metrics and scheduler logs. Will validate eviction timestamps against autoscaler events.
Maria Lopez (Customer, AtlasAI) 2026-03-10: Impacting user-facing production flows; saw retries and a few 503s in our logs. We can slow down warmup jobs if needed.

Drew Patel (SRE) 2026-03-11: Initial hypothesis: long-lived KV prefetches are growing host GPU memory footprint causing eviction cascade. Observed NVLink/PCIe io_wait correlated with eviction windows. Investigating autoscaler hysteresis settings.

Bethany Chang (Infra Eng) 2026-03-12: Reproduced locally with synthetic warmup pattern. Created temp patch to increase autoscale cooldown and prevent immediate shrink after scale-up. Patching to staging for validation.
investigation_notes: Observed recurring pattern every ~6 minutes where pool free_slots drop by 30-40% for ~90-180s.
Correlation matrix: eviction events align with host pcie_io_wait and host memory RSS growth on batch prefetcher processes.
Autoscaler logs show scale-up at t0+10s then scale-down decision within 60s due to quickly reduced request queue; cooldowns too short for long-tail workload.
Heap/kv cache growth: some KV-prefetch workers hold large contexts (8-12GB) longer than expected; GC not triggered until eviction threshold.
Confirmed no hardware faults; GPUs show normal temp and ECC counters. PCIe saturation likely due to many concurrent prefetch traffic and small-stream fanout.
Related runbook: nearline-gpu-contention-runbook indicated as reference; will adjust batching and prefetch TTLs.
resolution:
Workaround applied: Increased autoscaler cooldown to 4 minutes for dp-84a2 and applied temporary limit on concurrent KV-prefetch jobs (max 2). Customer advised to stagger warmup jobs. Post-change effects: eviction events dropped by 85% and p99 stabilized to pre-incident baseline.
Permanent plan: Implement autoscaler hysteresis heuristics to detect short-lived warmup spikes and avoid immediate shrink, add KV-prefetch TTL and memory caps per worker, and land PR to scheduler that defers eviction of warmup-prefetch allocations when queue is active. Scheduled rollout: autoscaler heuristic PR in staging by 2026-03-18, prod by 2026-03-24 after canary. Follow-ups: create alert for pcie_io_wait > 70% and add telemetry for KV-prefetch memory contribution.
